meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) Dec 2, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Charlie Reece convened the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) on December 2, 2020 alongside City Council members Javiera Caballero and Mark-Anthony Middleton, Durham County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Ellen Reckhow, and Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Busby. The committee honored outgoing County Commissioner Ellen Reckhow with a Resolution of Appreciation recognizing her three decades of public service and founding role on JCCPC, then unanimously approved the October 7, 2020 minutes 7-0. Planning staff presented updates on Comprehensive Plan draft objectives and bilingual outreach, early-alert notifications for annexation and rezoning cases, Expanding Housing Choices Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) permitting (~35 applications exceeding initial projections), and GIS Equity Indicators developed by intern Tyshawn Wooten and Kayla Seibel. Staff also clarified that recent community emails regarding the Durham Landscape Manual were supportive advocacy from coalition partners, and Chair Reece outlined the committee's upcoming February 2021 leadership transition before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call and Resolution of Appreciation for Commissioner Ellen Reckhow
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Charlie Reece called the meeting to order and confirmed attendance of all seven JCCPC members (Reece, Jacobs, Caballero, Reckhow, Middleton, Howerton, and Busby). Chair Reece read a formal Resolution of Appreciation honoring retiring County Commissioner Ellen Reckhow's three decades of service, followed by remarks from Reckhow, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Mark-Anthony Middleton.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 7, 2020 JCCPC Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following County and City Manager updates confirming no priority items from Mr. O'Toole or Mr. Wardell, JCCPC voted unanimously 7-0 to approve the October 7, 2020 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Update and Early Rezoning/Annexation Notifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Miller reported that draft Comprehensive Plan objectives were slated for release by month's end alongside English and Spanish community engagement tools. Chair Reece and staff discussed early-alert notifications to JCCPC and Council members when annexation or rezoning cases are filed in Southeast Durham and county areas.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choices / Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU) Monitoring Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Whiteman presented real-time monitoring data on ADU applications under Expanding Housing Choices, noting roughly 35 applications had already exceeded initial modest projections. Members praised tracking ordinance impacts in real time and discussed working with the local AIA chapter on template plans to make ADUs more affordable.

agenda_items.title: Equity Indicators GIS Project Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Sara Young introduced intern Tyshawn Wooten's GIS equity indicators work, presented by Kayla Seibel due to connection issues. Members reviewed initial datasets, accessible-language goals, and policy disparities exposed by the mapping—such as county subdivisions lacking sidewalk requirements—and reviewed proposed 2021 bimonthly meeting dates.

agenda_items.title: Durham Landscape Manual Public Emails Clarification and February 2021 Chair Transition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Commissioner Brenda Howerton's inquiry about community emails regarding the Durham Landscape Manual, Director Sara Young and Chair Charlie Reece clarified that environmental coalition partners were writing in strong support of adoption. Chair Reece concluded his final full meeting as chair by noting the February rotation norm elevating Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs to Chair and suggesting Mark-Anthony Middleton for Vice Chair.

votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) 7-member vote comprising 3 Durham City Council members, 3 Durham County Commissioners, and 1 Planning Commissioner.
votes.discussion_detail: County Commissioner Brenda Howerton moved and County Commissioner Ellen Reckhow seconded approving the October 7, 2020 JCCPC minutes. All seven JCCPC members (City Council members Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Mark-Anthony Middleton; County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Ellen Reckhow, and Brenda Howerton; and Planning Commissioner Busby) voted Aye, passing 7-0.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) Oct 7, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Council Member Charlie Reece alongside City Council members Javiera Caballero and Mark-Anthony Middleton, County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Ellen Reckhow, and Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Busby (with Pierce Freelon attending as City alternate), the Joint City-County Planning Committee met on October 7, 2020 and welcomed new Planning Director Sara Young. The committee approved its August 2020 minutes, heard Comprehensive Plan public engagement updates (including a Hispanic/Latino focus group, Engagement Ambassadors recruitment, and child-opportunity equity mapping), and received a briefing on technical Unified Development Ordinance amendments required by July 2021 under N.C.G.S. Chapter 160D. Members unanimously voted 7-0 to adopt Landscape Manual revisions promoting native plants and prohibiting invasive species in line with Durham's sustainability roadmap, and closed with an extensive discussion of the 2020 Industrial Land Use Study in which County Commissioners cautioned against reducing over 1,000 acres of industrial land before further vetting.

agenda_items.title: Welcome to Planning Director Sara Young and Approval of August 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Charlie Reece congratulated Sara Young on her appointment as Joint City-County Planning Director, and members noted Commissioner Ellen Reckhow's upcoming final JCCPC meeting. Commissioner Jacobs moved and Commissioner Reckhow seconded approval of the August 2020 minutes on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Engagement and Equity Mapping Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Lisa Miller and colleagues) reported on a late-September focus group for Hispanic and Latino residents facilitated with Carmen Ortiz, launch of Engagement Ambassadors recruitment, and coordination with the transit plan. Members also discussed equity mapping resources such as Wake County's Social Equity Atlas and diversitydatakids.org ahead of Future Land Use Map outreach.

agenda_items.title: N.C.G.S. Chapter 160D Unified Development Ordinance Technical Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Michael Stock briefed the committee on a primarily technical omnibus UDO text amendment consolidating municipal and county planning statutes under N.C.G.S. Chapter 160D ahead of the July 2021 statutory deadline. He noted 160D also simplifies governing-body consistency statement procedures for zoning map changes and text amendments.

agenda_items.title: Landscape Manual Revisions — Native Species and Invasive Plant Prohibitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following staff presentation by Danny Cultra and outreach from Audubon and environmental stakeholders, members praised the Landscape Manual updates for advancing Durham's sustainability roadmap by encouraging native plants where appropriate and prohibiting invasive species. Commissioner Jacobs moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded adopting the revisions, passing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2020 Industrial Land Use Study Presentation and Suitability Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Brooke Ganser presented the 2020 Industrial Land Use Study projecting roughly 43,000 industrial employees and 470 acres of industrial land demand by 2050, alongside a 0–14 suitability rubric identifying five most suitable areas. County Commissioners cautioned against cutting more than 1,000 industrial acres before further vetting given active RTP expansions (such as Corning and Merck), while Chair Charlie Reece asked staff to report suitability scores whenever rezoning proposals remove industrial land.

votes.notes: Joint committee vote: ayes lists seated City Council members on the roster (Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton); County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Ellen Reckhow, Brenda Howerton and Planning Commissioner Busby also sat as voting JCCPC members, with no opposition recorded.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Jacobs moved and Commissioner Reckhow seconded approving the August 2020 JCCPC minutes. Roll call began with Charlie Reece, Commissioner Jacobs, Javiera Caballero, and Commissioner Reckhow voting Aye before the remaining lines were truncated in the digest.

votes.item_title: Item 8 — Adopt Landscape Manual Revisions (Native Plants and Invasive Species Prohibition)
votes.notes: Joint committee 7-0 vote: ayes lists the three City Council voting members from SEATED_BOARD_ROSTER; County Commissioners Jacobs, Reckhow, Howerton and Planning Commissioner Busby also voted Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Jacobs moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded adopting the Landscape Manual revisions implementing sustainability roadmap protections. All seven JCCPC members voted Aye and the motion carried 7-0.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - August 5, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Durham City Council Member Charlie Reece on August 5, 2020, the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC)—including City Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton, Durham County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Ellen Reckhow, and Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Brian Busby—began by voting on a motion by Middleton, seconded by Busby, to grant an excused absence to Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson due to a hurricane-rescheduled work trip. Chair Reece and Commissioner Reckhow clarified prior meeting minutes to reflect that JCCPC had only reviewed a concept memo rather than draft zoning ordinance text on the controversial statutory development agreements text amendment. Planning staff Lisa Miller and Carl Kolosna updated the committee on Comprehensive Plan community engagement amid COVID-19, highlighting socially distanced 'Slow Streets' outreach on Benjamin Street with Spirit House. Later, JCCPC discussed 2017 state statutory limits on requiring developer off-site road improvements in Transportation Special Use Permits—with Chair Reece committing to draft a legislative delegation letter—and reviewed Omnibus 15 UDO text amendments covering TSUPs, Residential Compact (RC) transit-oriented density for future Bus Rapid Transit, RTP public-safety station setbacks, and riparian buffers.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, JCCPC Attendance, and Excused Absence for Mayor Pro Tempore Johnson
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee Chair Charlie Reece called the 9:30 a.m. JCCPC meeting to order with City Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton, County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Brian Busby present (and Commissioner Ellen Reckhow participating shortly thereafter). Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and Brian Busby seconded an excused absence for Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson, whose work trip was rescheduled due to the hurricane.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Roll Call; tally truncated in digest gap)

agenda_items.title: Clarification on Statutory Development Agreements Text Amendment Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In response to Commissioner Reckhow and public emails regarding statutory development agreements, Planning staff Michael Stock confirmed that JCCPC had previously reviewed only a conceptual memo rather than draft zoning ordinance text. Chair Charlie Reece requested that the minutes explicitly note no draft text was presented to JCCPC, while expressing confidence in ongoing Planning Commission and staff work.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Update — Equitable Community Engagement During COVID-19
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Lisa Miller and Carl Kolosna reported on adapting Comprehensive Plan engagement during COVID-19 while managing high development case volume. They highlighted resident outreach working groups, internet and home-environment barriers to Zoom meetings, and socially distanced in-person 'Slow Streets' events led by Spirit House (including Benjamin Street) where residents walked themes painted on the street and recorded goal statements.

agenda_items.title: TSUP Road Improvement Statutory Limits and Legislative Delegation Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a briefing with transportation staff (Bill) and the City Attorney's Office regarding a 2017 state statute and NCDOT financial constraints affecting developer road-improvement exactions, Chair Charlie Reece stated Durham needs local solutions rather than expecting near-term legislative relief. Chair Reece committed to circulating a draft letter to the legislative delegation after receiving staff details on two affected school projects.

agenda_items.title: Omnibus 15 Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Michael Stock presented Omnibus 15 UDO technical corrections and policy updates, seeking direction on removing redundant Transportation Special Use Permit (TSUP) triggers for 600+ peak-hour-trip uses where state law bars requiring uncompensated road improvements, updating the Residential Compact (RC) district from light rail to Bus Rapid Transit (20 units/acre), allowing EMS/fire stations in SRP/RTP to use Office & Institutional setbacks, and updating riparian and multi-zoning project boundary buffers. Committee members questioned potential indirect effects on BRT corridor density and asked why recent downtown projects (Geer Street and American Tobacco) did not use the affordable housing height bonus, which staff attributed anecdotally to financing challenges.

meetings.title: Virtual Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - June 3, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In the first virtual meeting of the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) on June 3, 2020, Planning Director Pat Young conducted the annual rotation of leadership, resulting in the election of City Council Member Charlie Reece as Chair (with Reece presiding thereafter alongside City Council Members Jillian Johnson and Mark-Anthony Middleton, County Commissioners Ellen Reckhow, Brenda Howerton, and Wendy Jacobs, and Planning Commissioner Miss Hammond). The committee unanimously elected Commissioner Wendy Jacobs as Vice Chair (7-0) and approved its February 4, 2020 minutes (7-0). Members received annual reports from the Appearance Commission, Board of Adjustment, and Durham Open Space and Trails Commission, emphasizing qualified board recruitment and active trail design. In policy review, JCCPC discussed a unified City-County UDO text amendment affirming binding Development Agreements (Item 10) and a supplemental amendment permitting virtual pre-application neighborhood meetings during emergency declarations, requesting greater precision on emergency triggers and earlier distribution of supplemental materials.

agenda_items.title: Election of JCCPC Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young oversaw the annual rotation of the JCCPC Chair from County Commissioner Ellen Reckhow to a City representative, and City Council Member Charlie Reece was nominated and elected Chair via roll call. After taking the gavel and apologizing for earlier rotation confusion, Chair Reece nominated BOCC Chair Wendy Jacobs as Vice Chair (seconded by Jillian Johnson); following a parliamentary inquiry by Mark-Anthony Middleton, the committee elected Jacobs 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Approval of February 4, 2020 JCCPC Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Charlie Reece called for corrections to the February 4, 2020 JCCPC minutes. On motion by Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton and second by Commissioner Brenda Howerton, the committee approved the minutes unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Annual Reports: Appearance Commission, Board of Adjustment, and DOST
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Liaisons reported on 2019–2020 activities of the Appearance Commission (Golden Leaf Awards, Chesterfield Building tour, and member departures), Board of Adjustment (attendance monitoring and difficulty recruiting qualified applicants, with Middleton emphasizing consistent qualified attendance), and Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (progress on Third Fork Creek and Belt Line trails).

agenda_items.title: Unified UDO Text Amendment: Development Agreements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff attorneys and planners Don O'Toole and Michael Stock presented a unified City-County UDO text amendment affirming statutory authority to negotiate binding, land-tied Development Agreements recorded with the Register of Deeds without adding uses prohibited by underlying zoning. Council Member Middleton asked about future boards' amendment powers and minimum acreage rules, while Commissioner Jacobs asked how Development Agreements compare with charter-restricted rezoning proffers.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: Virtual Neighborhood Meetings During Emergency Declarations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Sarah Young presented a time-sensitive UDO amendment allowing development applicants to hold required neighborhood meetings virtually when in-person gatherings are barred by an emergency declaration. Committee members criticized the late distribution of the supplemental packet and requested clearer language defining 'emergency declaration or other circumstances' before advancing to formal adoption.

votes.item_title: Election of Charlie Reece as JCCPC Chair
votes.notes: Roll call truncated in digest after Commissioner Ellen Reckhow ('Yes') and Council Member Jillian Johnson ('Yes') at [00:02:15]; Reece presided as Chair from [00:05:13] onward. City Council roster members on JCCPC were Charlie Reece, Jillian Johnson, and Mark-Anthony Middleton (serving alongside BOCC members Reckhow, Howerton, Jacobs, and Planning Commissioner Hammond).
votes.discussion_detail: Nominated and elected City Council Member Charlie Reece as JCCPC Chair under the annual City-County rotation.

votes.item_title: Election of Commissioner Wendy Jacobs as JCCPC Vice Chair
votes.notes: Full JCCPC roll call carried 7-0: City Council roster members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Mark-Anthony Middleton voted Aye alongside County Commissioners Ellen Reckhow, Brenda Howerton, and Wendy Jacobs and Planning Commissioner Miss Hammond.
votes.discussion_detail: Elected County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs as JCCPC Vice Chair following a parliamentary inquiry by Middleton on the rotation agreement.

votes.notes: Seconder was County Commissioner Brenda Howerton (not on City Council roster). Full JCCPC roll call carried 7-0 (City roster members Johnson, Reece, Middleton plus County/Planning members Reckhow, Howerton, Jacobs, and Hammond).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of the February 4, 2020 JCCPC meeting without revision.
